surface_mechanism_description: The ALD reaction mechanism involves two half-reactions: the first half-reaction is the surface reaction between the carbonyl precursor (W(CO)x*) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S), leading to the formation of surface-bound sulfide species (W–SH*) and the release of carbon monoxide (CO) and hydrogen (H2). The second half-reaction involves the reaction between the surface-bound sulfide species (W–SH*) and the second precursor (W(CO)6), resulting in the formation of a tungsten-sulfur-tungsten bond (W–S–W) and the release of CO and H2. The self-limiting nature of the ALD growth is confirmed by the saturation of the surface species after a certain number of precursor doses.
evidence: The two-half reaction mechanism was determined using in situ FTIR and RGA studies. The appearance and disappearance of characteristic FTIR peaks and the detection of by-products such as CO and H2 confirmed the surface reactions. The self-limiting nature of the ALD growth was further supported by the saturation of the surface species after a certain number of precursor doses.
